title: Providence, even over evil acts, is not confined to a general, indifferent concurrence
source_text: LVIII. Praesertim autem illud mihi certissimum est, quod etiam ab omnibus Theologis concedi puto, divinae providentiae vim & efficaciam, etiam circa actus malos, minime restringendam esse ad concursum quendam ex se generalem & indifferentem; sed Deum multis modis sapientiae ipsius cognitis, varios rerum eventus, etiam in quibus hominum malitia intervenit, procurare, promovere, dirigere atque moderari.
pass_a_gloss: But especially this is most certain to me, which I think is granted also by all Theologians, that the force and efficacy of divine providence, even about evil acts, is by no means to be restricted to a certain concurrence general of itself and indifferent; but that God in many ways known to his own wisdom, procures, promotes, directs and moderates various events of things, even those in which the malice of men intervenes.
pass_b_english: What I hold as most certain of all, and what I think all theologians grant, is that the power and efficacy of divine providence, even in regard to evil acts, must in no way be confined to a concurrence that is general and indifferent in itself.
In many ways known to his own wisdom, God brings about, furthers, directs and regulates the varied course of events, including those in which human wickedness plays a part.

lemmas.gloss: by no means to be restricted
in many ways known to his own wisdom

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
